title: Brightwell Health - SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review
next_steps: Priya to share latest SOC 2 Type II report and ISO mapping link by 2026-08-14
Alex to send pricing tiers and Dedicated vs Hosted comparison spreadsheet
Schedule follow-up deep-dive on KMS integration and customer KMS options (tentative 2026-08-18)
Customer to confirm list of systems requiring data residency restrictions by 2026-08-17
action_items: Priya Shah - Share SOC 2 Type II report PDF and controls mapping (due 2026-08-14)
Alex Moreno - Send Dedicated vs Hosted TCO spreadsheet and contract SOW template (due 2026-08-13)

summary: Redwood team reviewed SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture and how Redwood's Trust Center, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and KMS integrations meet Brightwell Health's requirements. Customer requested SOC 2 report, controls mapping, Trust Center access, and more detail on customer-managed KMS and data residency. Agreed next steps and follow-up deep-dive on KMS.
topics: Encryption at rest and KMS/HSM options
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. With me is Priya from our security engineering team and Daniel from CS. How's everybody today?
[00:06] Sophie Lane: Good, thanks. Sophie here — CISO at Brightwell. We have Mark and Rita on as well.
[00:10] Mark Delgado: Hey.
[00:12] Rita Gomez: Hi all.
[00:15] Priya Shah: Great — we'll run through SOC 2 and ISO posture, Trust Center links, KMS options, and then leave time for questions. Anything to add, Alex?
[00:22] Alex Moreno: Nope that's the plan. We're aiming for a practical mapping to your controls and to identify any gaps.
[00:27] Sophie Lane: Perfect. Quick context: we're finalizing a vendor security review for our LLM integrations team. We have strict data residency for PHI-adjacent telemetry, SOC 2 required, and we prefer customer-managed keys if possible.
[00:39] Priya Shah: Understood. At a high level Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering common criteria and a control set we can map to ISO 27001. We host a Trust Center with most supporting artifacts; we can give read-only access. For KMS we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS connectors, and we also have HSM integrations for Dedicated/Private deployments.
[01:02] Rita Gomez: When you say Trust Center, what exactly is there? Is the SOC 2 report downloadable?
[01:08] Daniel Wu: Yes — Trust Center has the SOC 2 Type II report (redacted as required), the ISO controls mapping summary, our pen test summary, security policies, and our vendor risk questionnaire responses. We can create a link to the Brightwell-specific folder.
[01:19] Sophie Lane: Do you provide evidence for controls? We need to see how controls map to our InfoSec framework and what evidence is available.
[01:26] Priya Shah: We provide a controls mapping spreadsheet that aligns SOC 2 trust services criteria to ISO 27001 Annex A controls and common customer frameworks. Evidence is often summarized in the mapping with references to policy docs and audit artifacts, and we can provide additional artifacts under NDA.
[01:40] Mark Delgado: On KMS, you mentioned customer-managed keys. Is that supported in the hosted product or only in Dedicated/Private?
[01:47] Priya Shah: Good question. For Hosted API customers we currently support Envelope Encryption with customer-provided keys via cloud KMS (AWS/GCP) — that requires a cross-account KMS grant and we can configure a key rotation policy. For Dedicated and Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM and integrate on-prem or in-VPC. There are some implementation notes around key escrow and auditability we'll share.
[02:08] Sophie Lane: Audit logs — we need immutable logs, 1 year retention for access events, and log forwarding to our SIEM. Can you forward logs to our Splunk or S3?
[02:18] Daniel Wu: Yes, we support log forwarding to S3, Splunk, and SIEMs via secure syslog/HTTPS ingestion. Audit trails include API calls, token-level operations, and admin activity. We also have write-once storage for critical audit artifacts in Dedicated deployments; for hosted there's an append-only audit store with tamper-evidence telemetry.
[02:36] Rita Gomez: How granular is RBAC? We need role separation between developers, ops, and security, and scoping down access to production data.
[02:43] Priya Shah: RBAC in the Console supports granular roles: reader, operator, auditor, admin, and custom roles. You can scope roles by project and model. SSO integrations are SAML2.0/OIDC, and we have out-of-box Okta templates. For programmatic access we use short-lived tokens and allow role-assumed service accounts.
[03:02] Sophie Lane: Do you support SCIM or automated user provisioning?
[03:05] Alex Moreno: We do support SCIM for user provisioning for enterprise plans; that's standard on Dedicated and Private and available on Hosted for enterprise customers.
[03:12] Mark Delgado: Data residency — we host in multiple regions, but can you guarantee that certain datasets never leave region X?
[03:19] Priya Shah: Yes — for Dedicated/Private or regional-hosted accounts we can pin processing and storage to a region (e.g., eu-west-1). For hosted accounts we offer region-specific tenancy in supported regions; we need to confirm the exact SLA and contract language but regional isolation is supported. We'll follow up with precise contractual wording.
[03:39] Sophie Lane: Regarding ISO 27001, do you have a certificate and can you show the scope?
[03:44] Daniel Wu: We have an ISO 27001 certificate for our control plane and selected hosting regions; the certificate scope is in the Trust Center. We'll provide the scoping statement and controls mapping.
[03:54] Sophie Lane: Any historical incidents or exceptions we should be aware of?
[03:58] Priya Shah: We disclose a summary of incidents and remediation in the security disclosure docs in Trust Center. Any major incidents are documented with root cause and mitigation; we can provide redacted writeups under NDA.
[04:10] Rita Gomez: For audit evidence, do you allow customer auditors to come on-site or do remote reviews only?
[04:16] Alex Moreno: For Hosted customers, we typically do remote evidence collection and a read-only Trust Center. For Dedicated/on-prem we can accommodate on-site reviews depending on contract and schedule.
[04:27] Mark Delgado: Does Redwood maintain SOC 2 continuously or is it annual?
[04:31] Daniel Wu: SOC 2 Type II is performed annually and covers an operating period in the report. We maintain continuous monitoring and update supporting materials as controls change.
[04:40] Sophie Lane: Encryption at rest — what algorithms and key lengths? Where are the keys stored?
[04:45] Priya Shah: Data at rest uses AES-256-GCM or equivalent. Keys are stored in KMS for hosted (Redwood-managed KMS or customer KMS) and can be in customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private. We rotate keys regularly and have documented rotation policies.
[04:58] Sophie Lane: Tokenization of PHI — do you offer tokenization or de-identification options on ingestion?
[05:04] Priya Shah: We have a pre-processing step customers can use (via our SDK or a routing proxy) to strip or tokenise PHI before it reaches the model. For regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private so that control of the ingest pipeline is fully in your environment.
[05:20] Alex Moreno: Quick pause — any other must-haves for you from a compliance perspective?
[05:24] Sophie Lane: We're tracking third-party subprocessor list, right to audit, breach notification timing, and ability to add contractual encryption requirements. Also we want clear mapping of Redwood controls to our internal control IDs.
[05:36] Priya Shah: We have a subprocessors list in the Trust Center and standard contract language for breach notification (48–72 hours initial notification) and right-to-audit clauses for enterprise contracts. We'll provide the controls mapping spreadsheet that references your control IDs if you share them.
[05:53] Mark Delgado: Network access controls — how do you handle egress and inbound restrictions for dedicated instances?
[05:59] Priya Shah: For Dedicated instances you get VPC peering, private endpoints, and optional egress restrictions. You can configure strict security groups and NAT gateway rules. We also support private deployments where all traffic remains within your network boundary.
[06:12] Rita Gomez: Logs retention policy — can we extend beyond 1 year? We might need 3—7 years for some audit artifacts.
[06:19] Daniel Wu: For Hosted we default to 1 year retention but can arrange extended retention as an add-on. For Dedicated we support customer-configured retention policies up to multi-year and export to long-term S3 buckets.
[06:33] Sophie Lane: On incident detection, do you integrate with our PagerDuty and what SLAs for detection/response?
[06:39] Daniel Wu: We integrate with PagerDuty for alerting, and provide a SOC-backed incident response process. SLA for incident acknowledgement can be part of an enterprise SLA; standard is 1-hour P1 ack for enterprise customers with premium SLA.
[06:53] Alex Moreno: Switching briefly to controls mapping — Priya, can you walk through an example mapping for access control?
[06:58] Priya Shah: Sure. For example, ISO A.9 / SOC 2 access control — we map provision/deprovision procedures, SSO/SCIM, MFA enforcement, and least privilege role templates. The mapping spreadsheet shows evidence like provisioning logs, policy docs, and a sample access review report.
[07:19] Sophie Lane: Will you be able to add our control IDs to that spreadsheet?
[07:22] Priya Shah: Yes if you send us a CSV of your control IDs, we'll add the mapping in our sheet.
[07:27] Mark Delgado: About pen tests — how recent and do you share full reports?
[07:31] Daniel Wu: We perform annual third-party pen tests and share executive summaries. Full reports can be shared under NDA.
[07:38] Rita Gomez: For legal, any standard exceptions in contracts for data residency?
[07:43] Alex Moreno: We can put strict residency clauses in SOWs for enterprise deals; that would go into the MSA/SOW negotiations. We'll surface sample contract language.
[07:51] Sophie Lane: Are there any limitations for encryption in transit for streaming responses?
[07:56] Priya Shah: No — all in-flight is TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; streaming uses secure websockets over TLS.
[08:03] Alex Moreno: Ok, let's open the floor for deeper questions. Mark?
[08:07] Mark Delgado: If we go with Hosted but need customer-managed keys, what is the operational impact and latency hit?
[08:13] Priya Shah: Envelope encryption adds a small latency on key unwrap — usually single-digit milliseconds. The bigger operational impact is cross-account KMS grants and audit configuration. For high-throughput workloads Dedicated might be more predictable. We'll share benchmarks.
[08:28] Sophie Lane: What about token-level attribution for cost/usage auditing — can we tie generated content back to users without leaking PII?
[08:36] Daniel Wu: Yes — we tag requests with tenant and token metadata. PII avoidance is a shared responsibility; we recommend pseudonymizing user identifiers and enabling our redaction hooks for stored logs.
[08:50] Rita Gomez: Do you keep model snapshots or fine-tuned artifacts? Policy on customer model artifacts?
[08:56] Priya Shah: By default we do not persist fine-tuned customer models in a shared way; in Dedicated/Private deployments, models and artifacts live within your tenancy and follow your retention rules. We'll clarify storage lifecycle policies.
[09:08] Sophie Lane: On governance, does Redwood have a dedicated security officer and formal risk register?
[09:13] Daniel Wu: Yes — we have a CISO organization and maintain a risk register and formal risk treatment plans.
[09:18] Mark Delgado: Is there a path to supporting hardware HSMs for key attestation?
[09:22] Priya Shah: Yes for Dedicated/Private we support HSM-backed key stores and attestation workflows. For Hosted we can integrate with cloud KMS-backed HSM services.
[09:33] Alex Moreno: We're at about 10 minutes in; want to make sure we hit your top concerns. Sophie?
[09:38] Sophie Lane: The main items are: SOC 2 report, Trust Center access, controls mapping including our control IDs, KMS options with architecture notes, and contractual residency language. Also documentation on audit log forwarding and retention.
[09:50] Alex Moreno: Great — those are all actionable. Priya will own the SOC 2 artifacts and controls mapping; Daniel will provision Trust Center access; Alex will follow up on contracting language and pricing.
[10:00] Mark Delgado: One more — do you provision separate tenants for test and prod by default?
[10:04] Priya Shah: Yes, we recommend separate projects/tenants for test and prod to prevent data bleed. For enterprise customers we can isolate networks further.
[10:12] Rita Gomez: For demos of Dedicated, can we see a network diagram and sample deployment?
[10:16] Alex Moreno: We'll include that in the follow-up package.
[10:19] Sophie Lane: On the Trust Center access, we'd prefer SSO-protected read-only access mapped to our compliance team.
[10:25] Daniel Wu: We can create a read-only role and sync to your Okta group. We support SCIM provisioning for that purpose.
[10:33] Priya Shah: Going back to evidence — we often provide sample policies and anonymized logs as examples; full artifacts require NDA.
[10:40] Sophie Lane: NDA is fine. We'll sign if needed.
[10:44] Alex Moreno: Quick note — for encryption key rotation, what's your policy expectations?
[10:48] Sophie Lane: We rotate keys annually and on compromise; we also require access logs for key use.
[10:54] Priya Shah: That aligns with our policy. We keep rotation logs and key usage audit trails; we can provide sample reports.
[11:02] Mark Delgado: Can you show the format of audit logs? Schema and fields? We need to map into our SIEM parser.
[11:08] Daniel Wu: We'll share the schema as JSON lines with examples and a Splunk ingestion guide.
[11:14] Rita Gomez: Are any subprocessors based in non-approved jurisdictions? We have strict vendor rules.
[11:19] Daniel Wu: Our subprocessors list includes cloud providers and some regional partners; we'll flag any that are in non-approved jurisdictions and discuss mitigations.
[11:28] Sophie Lane: About data deletion — can you certify deletion for a tenant?
[11:33] Priya Shah: We support data deletion APIs and documented retention workflows. For Hosted we provide a deletion certificate for major deletions; for Dedicated we provide deletion processes you can audit.
[11:44] Alex Moreno: Ok, we're around 35 minutes in — any final technical blockers?
[11:48] Mark Delgado: Not blockers, just need to review artifacts.
[11:51] Rita Gomez: We'll want the Trust Center link and the SOC 2 PDF.
[11:55] Daniel Wu: We'll provision that today and send the link.
[11:58] Sophie Lane: Timeline wise, we'd like to close vendor review in two weeks.
[12:02] Alex Moreno: Understood. We'll try to hit the dates on the action items.
[12:07] Priya Shah: Last note — for workloads that must never leave your VPC, we'll propose a Dedicated VPC deployment and an SOW for connectivity.
[12:16] Sophie Lane: That sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[12:18] Alex Moreno: Thanks — we'll recap and send follow-up.
[12:21] [END]
